questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English-speaking country as I'm studying English, close to Copenhagen and of cultural interest to me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, got a lot of emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance from the study abroad-team at my host university, they were super helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got lucky and found it easily. But I heard from others that it was super difficult.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Leases are often a whole year, but I made a deal with the landlord so it was no problem moving out after 4 months. But be aware that you could be committing to a whole year.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only downsides were the rent and the insulation of the buildings.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to go down and sign in physically, but it was easy. I booked a time slot and went down and got registered.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I think all kinds of help was available if you needed it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: just take it easy even though the amount of information can feel overwhelming. Just show up to what you have to and everything will be fine. Reach out to your guide if you need help with anything.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was fine and matched the level I'm used to from UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I liked the smaller seminars, but I did feel like I missed some critical texts and theory. I found out that all the other lit students were taking a course on reading theory, which I was not - so that would have been nice to know, as I often felt that the seminars were more about what we thought of the novels personally rather than us discussing them in relation to relevant theory/criticism.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Mystery and Horror, Body in Literature, Edinburgh in Fiction.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of the above, but I especially enjoyed mystery and horror. The instructor was great and the content was super interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None really.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is a bit less expensive than in DK. The same for restaurants and bars, which was really nice. Housing is definitely more expensive than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really join anything besides a sexual health club, they were great

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many. Erasmus had multiple parties, there were endless clubs/student societies - basically anything you could imagine, it was great.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining the Sexpression club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the isles! I went to the Isle of Skye and wish I could have gone again. Arran is accessible as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. People are so friendly and I loved the pub.culture, it's very much like in DK just a bit more chill.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Move into a flat outside of campus. I got friends for life this way, and they were truly such a big part of my exchange and daily life. It would not have been the same without them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and openness of the people in Edinburgh.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be open to new people and new experiences.
2. Hang out with your flatmates and let them show you around. 
3. Remember to do the things you think of doing - go out to the restaurants, go to the bars, go to the museums (many of them are free). Go to Arthur's seat, the seven hills of Edinburgh, go to the Pentlands, itøs so accessible!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My new friends. I got to meet so many amazing people because I kept an open mind. I connected with people from all over the world, and I'm super thankful for my new friends. It was not at all as scary as I thought it would be to be alone in a new place.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to go home again... I wish I could have stayed for 6 months at least.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
